signals.name: Michael Burry
signals.latest_title: Cassandra Unchained: Trading Post (Nov 5 and Nov 12 updates)
signals.summary: Per secondary reports, Burry sold 25% of his semiconductor ETF puts after a sharp Nov 5 drop but says he remains very bearish. On Nov 12 he reportedly used a Nasdaq 100 bounce off 27,000 to double his put position. These come from news coverage of his paid Substack, not his posts directly.
signals.connection: Bearish chip and AI positioning set against Nvidia's record $115.8B quarter and the Fed hawkishness from hot CPI.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.latest_title: Apple Permissions Update, The New App Paradigm, My iPhone Duo Review
signals.summary: On Nov 17 he argued Apple isn't ruining the Mac but isn't solving the agent problem, and questioned whether it can think outside the app paradigm. His Nov 16 'Obituaries' and the Nov 13 weekly 'The End of Jensen' piece cover the demise of Jensen Huang and what it means for Nvidia's long-term prospects, the AI bubble, and how the U.S. views itself.
signals.connection: Directly relevant to today's Nvidia record-quarter story, since he frames Huang's exit as a turning point for Nvidia and the AI cycle. The agent and app-paradigm piece ties to frontier AI and applied tech.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.summary: On Nov 11 he wrote on cycles, bubbles and the golden age of consumer surplus. His Nov 13 Weekly Dose of Optimism #219 rounds up AlphaGenome 2, Unnatural Products x Argenx, SpaceX Solar, Voyager 1 and more. Only the RSS blurbs were available, not the full text.
signals.connection: His bubbles-and-moats framing bears on the debate over Nvidia's record quarter and whether the AI boom is a bubble. The optimism roundup covers frontier tech.

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: How I fight token fraud as a solo founder
signals.summary: His Nov 16 How I AI episode (40 min) walks through six token-fraud attack patterns, the defenses built after losing tens of thousands of dollars, and why the guest killed free trials. The same week's roundup includes a Fable 5.2 review and a Claude Code family OS. The other Nov 17 post is a promo for free tools, which I skipped.
signals.connection: Ties to frontier AI and applied tech, covering the practical costs and risks of running AI products.
